title: The Narasimha Purana
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vyasa; the Narasiṃha Purāṇa is one of the shorter Puranas, a Vaishnava compilation of northern India whose contents overlap the Vishnu Purana and the Vishnudharmottara. GRETIL's e-text follows Siddheswar Jena's edition (Delhi 1987).
description: The Narasiṃha Purāṇa is the Purana of the man-lion: drawn from older material on Vishnu's avatars, it narrates the deeds of the boar, the dwarf and above all Narasiṃha, the avatars of the fish and the tortoise, the churning of the ocean, the genealogies of the solar and lunar houses, and the killing of Hiranyakashipu, and with the stories it treats the worship of Vishnu, the sacred days and months, the duties of the castes and stages of life, and the practice of repeating the divine name.
historicalContext: Its chapters on the avatars and on the calendar of vows were used by the Vaishnava communities of north India and by the compilers of later Puranic anthologies; the text is a witness to how the narrative Puranas were reworked into manuals of devotion and observance.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: 68 chapters and 3,507 verses, streamed from GRETIL at read time. Each passage is one verse, addressed as chapter.verse.
